lens: Proposal B — Decision-centric. Stages and sub-stages are derived bottom-up by clustering the ~98 concrete decision points and ~150 intervention surfaces from the evidence into 'decision families', then carving the minimal set of stages such that (a) each family sits inside exactly one stage and (b) every stage boundary coincides with a named hook point that ALL THREE decompilers independently expose (Ghidra group tags + root-action variants, angr ClinicStage 0-15 / OptimizationPassStage 0-11, Reko AnalysisStage PreSsa/AfterRegisterSsa/AfterStackSsa/AfterExpressionCoalescing + IAnalysisFactory). The taxonomy is an LLM-agent-facing catalog: each sub-stage names the exact assertion that changes its outcome and how each decompiler accepts (or fails to accept) that assertion today. Decision points with no override path are flagged as 'latent sub-stages' = kuna development opportunities.
executive_summary: The prior 19-stage list fails because it is a compiler's feed-forward spine (Loader→Decode→Lift→SSA→Types→Structuring→Render) bolted onto a system whose defining property is that almost every artifact is provisional and gets rewritten when a later stage learns something. Working bottom-up from the evidence, the ~98 decision points cluster into ~11 'decision families' that do not align with compiler phases but with three things the decompiler actually commits to and later revises: WHAT-IS-CODE (flow/switch/inline), WHAT-IS-A-DEFINITION (SSA heritage + dead-code gating), WHAT-IS-A-CALL (prototype/param/return trials), WHAT-IS-A-VARIABLE (stack/merge/alias), WHAT-IS-A-TYPE (inference + locks), and WHAT-IS-THE-SHAPE (structuring/goto/cast/emit). Crucially the boundaries between these families are EXACTLY the named hook points all three tools evolved — proving the families are real, not imposed. So I propose 8 first-pass-ordered stages keyed by owned artifact (S1 Reachable-Code Graph, S2 SSA/Definition Web, S3 Call & Prototype Model, S4 Variable & Storage Model, S5 Type Lattice Solution, S6 Region Hierarchy, S7 Structured AST, S8 Surface Text), wrapped by S0 (Loaded Image + Persistent Assertion Store) which is not a processing stage but the durable knowledge store every feedback edge writes to and every (re-)run reads from. The novelty over the old list: (1) the 19 stages collapse because 'Simplify/Dataflow/SSA/Calls/Stack/Memory/ScalarTypes/AggregateTypes/Variables/Range/Interproc' are not stages at all — they are sub-stages and fixed-point iterations INSIDE S2-S5 that the evidence shows interleaving in a single quiescence loop (Ghidra mainloop, angr Clinic 4x simplify, Reko SccWorker ~15 transforms); (2) feedback is first-class as 9 typed edges, not an afterthought; (3) every sub-stage carries an assertion type, and ~30% of decision points are LATENT (hardcoded, no override) which is precisely kuna's product surface. This refines H4 (artifact-keyed is right) but corrects H1 (5 mechanisms is too few — the evidence needs at least the local-fixpoint, intra-stage-iteration, persisted-restart, KB-reflow, and speculate-rollback types PLUS a 'worklist re-enqueue' type and a 'lazy-dirty recompute' type) and H2/H3 (the hook points align but Ghidra's hooks are coarser than angr's, so one Ghidra group often spans two angr ClinicStages — the taxonomy must take the FINER grain).

stages.name: Loaded Image & Persistent Assertion Store
stages.artifact: Image+SegmentMap+SymbolDB/KB/Program.User (the durable override store that survives every restart and re-decompile)
stages.description: Not a processing stage in the first-pass sense; it is the substrate. It owns the loaded bytes, segment/symbol map, architecture/platform/calling-convention models, and — most importantly for this taxonomy — the persistent assertion store that all feedback edges write into and every (re-)run of S1-S8 reads from on entry. This is the formal home of H3's 'durable assertions, never imperative mid-pipeline edits'. The three decompilers each have exactly one such store (Ghidra Symbol DB + Override + deadcodedelay; angr KnowledgeBase + DecompilationCache + variables_with_manual_types; Reko Program.User.*). It is listed as a stage because the decision of WHICH loader/arch/platform/load-address is itself an intervention surface that re-keys everything downstream, and because making it explicit is what lets us model non-linearity as 'edge writes to S0, then a scoped subset of S1-S8 re-runs reading S0'.

substages.name: Loader / architecture / platform selection
substages.decision: Which IImageLoader, processor model, and ABI/calling-convention set govern decoding. Changes the byte-to-instruction map and every register/stack model downstream.
substages.intervention: Assertion: loader/arch/platform override. Reko: User.Loader/User.Processor/User.Environment (exposed). Ghidra: Architecture chosen by caller/spec files (exposed at tool level). angr: project-level, mostly fixed per-project (partial).

substages.name: Assertion-store admission policy
substages.decision: Which user/LLM facts are treated as ground truth vs hints, and whether a given assertion clears the cache / forces restart vs only reflows output. This decision governs the SCOPE of every feedback edge.
substages.intervention: Assertion: per-fact lock/clears_cache flag. angr: DecompilationOption.clears_cache + mark_manual=True (exposed, fine-grained). Ghidra: typelock/namelock/isolate flags + Override entries (exposed but coarse — any change re-runs full pipeline). Reko: Program.User.* are all admitted, no per-fact cache policy (LATENT — kuna opportunity to make admission policy first-class).

stages.name: Reachable-Code Graph Recovery
stages.artifact: P-code/AIL/RTL CFG over the set of addresses decided to be code (Ghidra Funcdata dead-list+bblocks; angr clinic AIL graph; Reko ControlGraph+RtlBlocks)
stages.description: Owns the answer to 'what bytes are code, where do basic blocks begin/end, and where does control flow go' — including the hardest sub-problems: indirect-branch/jump-table modeling, call-vs-branch classification, and inline/inject decisions. This is the cluster of the 'flow-following policy' and 'switch model selection' decision families. It is a single stage because Ghidra's frontend (flow.cc/generateOps+generateBlocks) , angr's AIL creation + indirect-jump/tailcall fixups, and Reko's recursive-descent Scanner all own this artifact and all expose a worklist (Ghidra tablelist/injectlist/addrlist; angr opt-passes AFTER_AIL_GRAPH_CREATION; Reko procQueue) plus a jump-table sub-system that re-enqueues. The old list's 'Loader/Decode/P-code Lift/Disassembly/IR Containers' (5 stages) collapse here because they are feed-forward steps with no independent decision surface — the only decisions are flow-following ones, and they all feed the same artifact.

substages.name: Flow-following / error-mode policy
substages.decision: On unimplemented/bad/out-of-bounds/too-many-instructions, truncate-with-HALT vs throw vs ignore. Decides how much of the function exists at all.
substages.intervention: Assertion: flow option flags. Ghidra: flowoptions bitmap + setMaximumInstructions (exposed). angr: largely fixed (LATENT). Reko: User.Patches for specific bad instructions (exposed, per-address).

substages.name: Switch / jump-table model selection
substages.decision: Which JumpModel (Basic, Basic2, Trivial, Assisted, Override) explains a BRANCHIND, table base/stride/bounds, and case count. Wrong choice loses cases or fabricates edges; directly sets switch vs goto downstream.
substages.intervention: Assertion: explicit jump table. Ghidra: JumpBasicOverride via setOverride + Override.insertMultistageJump (exposed). Reko: User.IndirectJumps/User.JumpTables (exposed, richest). angr: jump-table is an opt-pass with no per-table user table input (LATENT — kuna opportunity).

substages.name: Call-vs-branch / inline / inject classification
substages.decision: Is a CALL really a tail-branch (PIC/thunk)? Should a callee be inlined or replaced by an inject payload? Pulls callee code into the artifact or not.
substages.intervention: Assertion: flow override + inline/inject directive. Ghidra: Override.insertFlowOverride/insertIndirectOverride + FuncProto.isInline + PcodeInjectLibrary (exposed). angr: inline_functions set (exposed). Reko: thunk/promote heuristics are hardcoded (Scanner.cs:474-479) (LATENT).

substages.name: Reachability pruning
substages.decision: Whether unreachable blocks (post call-to-branch, post-truncation, post-determined-branch) are removed or kept with warning.
substages.intervention: Assertion: possible_unreachable handling. Ghidra: removeUnreachableBlocks gated by flag (semi-exposed). Reko: AggressiveBranchRemoval heuristic (exposed via User.Heuristics). angr: DeadblockRemover BEFORE_REGION_IDENTIFICATION (pass on/off via preset).

stages.name: Definition Web (Heritage / SSA) & Dead-Definition Gate
stages.artifact: SSA-form value graph: varnodes/vvars/SSA-ids linked to defining ops, phi/MULTIEQUAL nodes, and the per-space heritage coverage map
stages.description: Owns 'what is a definition and which use reads which definition', i.e. SSA construction plus the dead-code-removal gating that is inseparable from it. This is the 'heritage staging' and 'dead-definition delay' decision family. It is one stage even though it iterates heavily, because all three tools treat SSA+deadcode as a coupled fixed point keyed to ONE artifact: Ghidra heritages per-space across passes and DELAYS deadcode until a space is fully heritaged (deadcodedelay), bumping+restarting when new varnodes appear; angr does two-level SSA (L0 register, L1 stack) with simplify passes between; Reko does Braun-Buchwald-Hack SSA with RenameFrameAccesses re-runs as new stack vars appear. The old list's 'Simplify/Dataflow/SSA' are not three stages — Simplify and Dataflow are the rule-pool/value-propagation FIXED POINTS inside this stage's quiescence loop. Note angr's two SSA levels are why this stage's boundary with S4 is fuzzier in angr than Ghidra (see hypothesis critique).

substages.name: Heritage staging / space delay order
substages.decision: Per-address-space order and initial delay of heritage (e.g. stack delay=1 to collect all stack varnodes before linking). Decides phi placement completeness.
substages.intervention: Assertion: per-space heritage delay. Ghidra: HeritageInfo.delay (LATENT at user level — only architecture spec sets it). angr: the L0/L1 split is the analogous staging, fixed (LATENT). kuna opportunity: expose staging order.

substages.name: Dead-definition delay / removal gate
substages.decision: Whether dead-code removal for a space is allowed yet (pass > deadcodedelay). Premature removal loses real definitions; this is the canonical persisted-restart trigger.
substages.intervention: Assertion: deadcodedelay override. Ghidra: Override.insertDeadcodeDelay (exposed, per-space). angr: remove_dead_memdefs option (exposed, coarse boolean). Reko: hardcoded DeadCode.Eliminate ordering (LATENT).

substages.name: Range refinement / phi granularity
substages.decision: Whether to split a memory range at gaps before placing phis (Ghidra size>4 && max<size heuristic). Affects how precisely large/overlapping storage is tracked.
substages.intervention: Assertion: none today. Ghidra hardcoded threshold 4 (heritage.cc:2610) (LATENT — kuna opportunity, esp. for struct-heavy stack frames).

substages.name: Value-propagation / simplification quiescence
substages.decision: Which algebraic/peephole rules fire and when the fixed point is declared (Ghidra oppool1 repeat; angr 4x simplify + BlockSimplifier 30-cap; Reko VP+CCE+Coalescer loops). Determines expression shape fed to typing and structuring.
substages.intervention: Assertion: per-rule enable/disable. Ghidra: OptionToggleRule + Rule::setDisable (exposed). angr: peephole_optimizations list (exposed). Reko: ExpressionSimplifier rules statically instantiated (LATENT).

stages.name: Call & Prototype Model
stages.artifact: Per-call and per-function FuncCallSpecs/prototype: parameter list, return value(s), calling convention, preserved/trashed sets, extrapop
stages.description: Owns 'what is the signature of this function and of everything it calls', recovered via trial-and-refinement. This is the 'prototype trial finalization' and 'interprocedural summary' decision family. It is its own stage (not folded into S2) because it has a distinct artifact, a distinct iteration unit (ParamActive trial passes / angr callsite construction twice / Reko SCC bottom-up summaries), and a distinct intervention surface (locked prototypes). Critically it is bidirectionally coupled to S2/S5: param trials read the SSA web, and a locked prototype invalidates trials and can force restart. The old list had this as one feed-forward 'Calls/Interproc' box; the evidence shows it is an iterative, interprocedural fixed point (Reko's SCC model is the clearest: callee summaries flow UP to callers within an SCC).

substages.decision: Use a declared/locked signature (skip recovery) or run iterative trial recovery. Decides whether downstream sees exact or guessed params.

substages.name: Trial finalization threshold
substages.decision: How many refinement passes before param/return trials are frozen (Ghidra maxpass; angr two-pass callsite; Reko convergence). Trades accuracy vs speed and decides borderline params in/out.

substages.name: Calling-convention / ABI trust
substages.decision: Trust the platform ABI for preserved/trashed registers vs infer from dataflow. Changes liveness and thus which params/returns exist.

substages.decision: Stack adjustment across each call when underdetermined (StackSolver linear system). Wrong delta corrupts caller stack-var recovery in S4.

stages.name: Variable & Storage Model
stages.artifact: HighVariables / unified SimVariables / Reko webs: the mapping from SSA values + storage locations to named program variables, plus stack-frame layout and alias sets
stages.description: Owns 'which SSA values are the same program variable, what is the stack frame layout, and what aliases what'. This is the 'merge aggressiveness', 'stack restructuring', and 'alias/dynamic-mapping' decision family. Distinct artifact (HighVariable/unified var) and distinct intervention (isolate, rename, stack symbol). In Ghidra this is the post-cleanup merge phalanx (ActionMerge*) plus ActionRestructureVarnode; in angr it is VariableRecoveryFast + unify_variables(liveness); in Reko it is WebBuilder + ComplexStackVariableTransformer. The old list split this into 'Stack/Memory/Variables' — but the evidence shows merging, stack layout, and aliasing co-determine each other and share the variable artifact, and stack-restructuring feeds back into type inference (S5) and back into itself.

substages.name: Merge aggressiveness (required vs speculative vs adjacent)
substages.decision: Which SSA values collapse into one variable. Forced merges are semantic; speculative merges are heuristic and can wrongly fuse unrelated values.
substages.intervention: Assertion: per-variable isolate / merge hint. Ghidra: Symbol setIsolated (exposed, prevents speculative merge). angr: variable identity via kb.variables (exposed via rename). Reko: web building hardcoded (LATENT).

substages.name: Stack-frame layout / RangeHint conflict resolution
substages.decision: How overlapping stack ranges resolve to symbols (typelock > rangeType > type specificity). Decides struct vs scalars on the frame.
substages.intervention: Assertion: stack symbol + type lock. Ghidra: ScopeLocal symbols + RangeHint typelock (exposed via Symbol DB). angr: static_buffers + manual stack var types (exposed). Reko: User.Globals for globals; stack layout LATENT.

substages.name: Alias / dynamic-storage policy
substages.decision: Which storage overlaps are treated as aliasing (AliasChecker boundaries), and binding of per-location facets to ephemeral temporaries.
substages.intervention: Assertion: union-facet / dynamic-hash symbol. Ghidra: UnionFacetSymbol via DynamicHash (exposed). angr/Reko: LATENT.

substages.name: Explicit-vs-implied / variable visibility
substages.decision: Whether a variable is its own named token or inlined into a parent expression. Pure readability, no semantics — but huge output impact.
substages.intervention: Assertion: none per-variable in Ghidra (heuristic-only, LATENT). angr: expr_collapse_depth (exposed, global). kuna opportunity: per-variable force-explicit assertion.

stages.name: Type Lattice Solution
stages.artifact: Datatype assigned to every variable/expression: the solved type constraint system including reconstructed structs/unions/arrays
stages.description: Owns 'what is the type of each value'. This is the 'type-flow direction', 'union field scoring', 'type-lock enforcement', and 'aggregate reconstruction' decision family. Distinct artifact and distinct solver. The split between Ghidra (iterative per-edge propagation, 7-pass cap, bidirectional within the cap, tightly coupled to S4 via spacebase-relative pointer feedback) and angr/Reko (collect constraints once, solve as a separate union-find/Typehoon problem, seed ground truth from locks) is the single biggest architectural divergence in the evidence and the place where the artifact-keyed model pays off: in all three, S5 reads S2/S4 and writes types that can re-trigger S4 (Ghidra ActionRestructure) and S3 (prototype refinement). The old list's 'ScalarTypes/AggregateTypes/Range' three boxes are sub-stages here (Range/value-set analysis is an input to typing and to S1 switch bounds, not a standalone stage).

stages.name: Region Hierarchy Recovery
stages.artifact: Region/block-structure tree: loops, single-entry regions, dominator/post-dominator hierarchy with edges classified as structurable vs virtualized/goto
stages.description: Owns 'what is the nesting hierarchy of control flow' — distinct from S7 (the schema-matched AST) because the evidence shows region identification is a separate, re-runnable artifact that graph-editing passes invalidate (angr makes this explicit: any DURING_REGION_IDENTIFICATION graph edit re-runs RegionIdentifier). This is the 'loop refinement', 'single-exit enforcement', and 'edge virtualization heuristic' decision family. Ghidra fuses S6 into ActionBlockStructure/CollapseStructure, but the evidence (block structure computed twice, pre- and post-merge) shows the hierarchy is a distinct artifact even there. The old list folded all of structuring into one 'Structuring' box; splitting S6 from S7 is what makes the speculate-validate-rollback feedback edge (SAILR) expressible: it edits the graph (S1/S6 artifact), re-runs S6, re-structures S7, measures goto/quality, and rolls back.

This is the 'structuring schema precedence', 'goto placement/minimization', and 'switch-vs-if-cascade' decision family. Separated from S6 because the schema-matcher consumes the region hierarchy and produces a different artifact (AST), and because the post-structuring simplification + quality measurement live here and drive the rollback edge back to S6. angr exposes AFTER_STRUCTURING passes; Ghidra runs CollapseStructure (greedy ordered rules) then RegionSimplifier-equivalent cleanup; Reko has its IfCascadeToSwitch/ForLoop/TailReturn post-processors.

substages.name: Goto placement & quality acceptance
substages.decision: Which residual edges become gotos, and whether a de-optimization that changes goto count is accepted (SAILR prevent_new_gotos / must_improve_rel_quality). This is the speculate-rollback decision.
substages.intervention: Assertion: per-edge force-goto (S6 surface) + quality policy. angr: StructuringOptimizationPass params prevent_new_gotos/strictly_less_gotos/must_improve_rel_quality (exposed per-pass). Ghidra: force-goto only (exposed); quality policy hardcoded (LATENT).

substages.name: Switch-vs-if-cascade & for-loop recognition
substages.decision: Whether an if-else chain is rewritten to a switch and whether a while is recognized as a for. Pure readability vs fidelity.
substages.intervention: Assertion: structuring options. angr: simplify_ifelse/use_multistmtexprs (exposed). Ghidra: OptionAnalyzeForLoops (exposed). Reko: always-on (LATENT).

stages.name: Surface Lowering & Text Emission
stages.artifact: Final source text plus position/instruction maps: variable names, casts, constant formats, NULL keyword, declarations
stages.description: Owns 'the rendered code': naming, cast insertion policy, constant formatting, declaration placement. This is the 'naming policy', 'cast policy', and 'literal-format' decision family. It is the only stage that is genuinely close to feed-forward (it rarely feeds back into analysis) — but it is NOT trivial because it has the densest set of pure-display intervention surfaces and is the target of the KB-reflow edge (angr reflow re-runs S5→S8 only) and the LLM-refine edge (renames/types re-render S8, optionally re-seeding S5). The old list's 'C Lowering/C Render' two boxes collapse here; semantic naming (angr) and ActionNameVars (Ghidra) are sub-stages.
stages.ghidra_evidence: coreaction.cc:5891 ActionNameVars, 5892 ActionSetCasts; cast.cc CastStrategyC; printc.cc (OptionNullPrinting/OptionIntegerFormat/OptionNoCastPrinting); Symbol namelock + displayFormat.
stages.angr_evidence: structured_codegen/c.py; semantic naming orchestrator (clinic.py SEMANTIC_VARIABLE_NAMING=14); decompiler.py:468-484 codegen + 493-501 llm_refine; expr_comments/const_formats; reflow_variable_types re-renders without re-analysis.
stages.reko_evidence: AbsynStatementEmitter.cs; TypeFormatter; GlobalDataWriter; ComplexTypeNamer (naming happens in S5 but applied here); DeclarationInserter.

substages.name: Naming policy
substages.decision: Auto-generated vs symbol-derived vs semantic-pattern names; whether to preserve user names.
substages.intervention: Assertion: name lock / explicit name. Ghidra: Symbol namelock (exposed). angr: var.name + var.renamed=True (exposed) + semvar_naming toggle. Reko: User.Procedures/User.Globals names (exposed).

substages.name: Cast emission policy
substages.decision: Minimal-necessary vs always vs never casts. Pure display, but governs correctness-of-recompilation perception.
substages.intervention: Assertion: cast option. Ghidra: OptionNoCastPrinting (exposed, global). angr: show_casts (exposed). Per-expression cast control LATENT everywhere.

substages.name: Literal / format policy
substages.decision: Integer base, NULL-vs-0, per-symbol display format.
substages.intervention: Assertion: format option. Ghidra: OptionIntegerFormat/OptionNullPrinting + per-Symbol displayFormat (exposed, both global and per-symbol). angr: const_formats (exposed, per-location). Reko: LATENT.

feedback_edges.trigger_signal: jump-table target / data code-pointer / inline-clone produces a new code address
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: tablelist/injectlist/addrlist re-enqueued within one generateOps call (flow.cc:781-805, 1058-1083). Reko: VectorBuilder/Backwalker EnqueueJumpTarget at PriorityJumpTarget; DataScanner code-pointer→EnqueueImageSymbol (Scanner.cs:309-314,1065-1118). angr: jump-table recovery as DURING_RI pass adds blocks. This is NOT H1's local-fixpoint nor staged-re-entry — it is a work-queue that grows; the unit re-processed is an address, not a stage.

feedback_edges.trigger_signal: multistage jump-table size mismatch (partial table size != recovered size) detected after simplification
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: jumptable.cc:2712-2717 matchModel → Override.insertMultistageJump + setRestartPending → ActionRestartGroup clears analysis and re-runs from fullloop start with the multistage hint persisted in S0 (action.cc:553-582). The hint survives the restart; the re-run reads it from the Override store.

feedback_edges.mechanism_type: local fixed-point within a stage (H1a) AND intra-stage iteration (refined H1)
feedback_edges.trigger_signal: a simplification rule fires / value propagation changes a varnode (count>lcount)
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: oppool1 131 rules repeat (action.cc:877-888) and the whole mainloop repeats on any change (coreaction.cc:5636). angr: BlockSimplifier while-loop max 30 (block_simplifier.py:130-150) + 4x _simplify_function. Reko: ValuePropagator+ConditionCodeEliminator loop (SccWorker.cs:210-212), Coalescer+VP+DeadCode (DataFlowAnalysis.cs:275-286). Distinguish the rule-pool fixpoint (a) from the action-group quiescence iteration (a coarser intra-stage loop).

feedback_edges.mechanism_type: global restart with persisted hint (H1c) — deadcode delay
feedback_edges.trigger_signal: a free varnode appears at an address already heritaged AND deadcode was removed for that space
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: heritage.cc:2712-2730 detect → bumpDeadcodeDelay (insertDeadcodeDelay+1 into Override store) + setRestartPending → whole-function restart with the incremented delay persisted (heritage.cc:2571-2581). Gated off during jumptable recovery (isJumptableRecoveryOn).

feedback_edges.trigger_signal: type inference assigns/refines a spacebase-relative pointer type, changing the implied stack struct layout
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: coreaction.cc:968-984 — ActionInferTypes propagateSpacebaseRef changes local-map struct types, marks ActionRestructureVarnode dirty (numpass++), which re-runs and feeds types back into the next inference iteration; an explicit acknowledged loop with an arbitrary iteration cap (line 972). This is the clearest S5↔S4 bidirectional edge.

feedback_edges.trigger_signal: prototype changes (trial finalization or lock) alter param/return varnodes
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: proto actions setRestartPending → ActionRestartGroup re-runs fullloop so heritage/typing see the new signature (coreaction.cc:5630-5647, action.cc:553-582). Reko: SCC bottom-up — callee summary (preserved/trashed/used) flows up, CallRewriter rewrites caller call sites, changing caller liveness/SSA reads (DataFlowAnalysis.cs:129-177).

feedback_edges.trigger_signal: HighVariable merge changes a variable's cover/type/symbol membership
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: variable.hh:120-152 coverdirty/typedirty/symboldirty flags set on merge; cover/type recomputed lazily on next access rather than by re-running a stage. This is a distinct mechanism from re-entry — the recompute is demand-driven and scoped to one object, not a pass re-run. angr unify_variables is by contrast one-pass (no dirty loop), highlighting the divergence.

feedback_edges.trigger_signal: a DURING_REGION_IDENTIFICATION de-optimization edits the graph; post-structuring goto count / loop-quality measured against the pre-edit baseline
feedback_edges.examples: angr: StructuringOptimizationPass edits graph → _recover_regions re-runs S6 (decompiler.py:646-657) → re-structure S7 → ControlFlowStructureCounter + GotoManager checked; if gotos increased or for-loops degraded to while, out_graph discarded and _prev_graph restored (optimization_pass.py:546-587, 662-724). DuplicationReverter max_opt_iters=5. The single richest non-linearity in the corpus; Ghidra/Reko have NO equivalent rollback (they greedily emit gotos), which is a kuna opportunity.

feedback_edges.trigger_signal: a schema match modifies the region graph mid-pass
feedback_edges.examples: angr: phoenix.py GraphChangedNotification (59) caught in _analyze_acyclic, resets idx=0 and restarts schema matching from scratch (1256-1292). Ghidra: CollapseStructure collapseInternal worklist re-evaluates blocks after each successful rule (blockaction.cc:1787-1870). Reko: StructureAnalysis do-while until regionGraph.Nodes<=1 or 1000-iter cap (StructureAnalysis.cs:143-186).

feedback_edges.mechanism_type: outer re-decompilation against persistent KB — narrow reflow (H1d)
feedback_edges.trigger_signal: user/LLM writes a manual type (mark_manual=True) into the assertion store and requests a reflow, not a full re-decompile
feedback_edges.examples: angr: reflow_variable_types (decompiler.py:699-830) re-seeds Typehoon ground_truth from variables_with_manual_types and re-runs ONLY S5→S8, reusing cached S1-S4 (clinic). This proves feedback edges have SCOPE: the same KB edit can trigger a narrow (S5+) or full (S1+) re-run depending on which artifact it invalidates.

feedback_edges.mechanism_type: outer re-decompilation against persistent KB — full (H1d)
feedback_edges.trigger_signal: user/LLM edit invalidates a cache-clearing assertion (proto lock, override, clears_cache=True option, force-goto)
feedback_edges.examples: Ghidra: any Symbol/Override edit → next decompile() loads fresh store and runs full pipeline; clearAnalysis purges cached state (action.cc:574). angr: option with clears_cache=True invalidates DecompilationCache → full Clinic re-run (decompiler.py:151-173,224-229). Reko: OnLoadedScript mutates User.Procedures → ScanProceduresRecursively re-enqueues (Decompiler.cs:629-649). The 'edit store, re-run everything' loop is the master feedback edge of all three tools.

intervention_model: Interventions are modeled as TYPED ASSERTIONS written to the S0 store, each carrying (scope, target-artifact, lock-strength), consulted by the owning sub-stage on every (re-)run. This directly operationalizes H3 ('durable assertions, never imperative mid-pipeline edits') and is confirmed by all three tools storing facts out-of-band (Ghidra Symbol DB + Override; angr KB variables_with_manual_types + DecompilationOption.clears_cache; Reko Program.User.*). The model has four parts. (1) Assertion type: each sub-stage above names exactly one assertion type that overrides it (e.g. S1.switch→explicit-jump-table, S2.deadcode→deadcodedelay, S3.proto→locked-prototype, S5.type→type-lock/ground-truth, S6.goto→force-goto-edge, S8.name→name-lock). (2) Lock strength: HARD (blocks all inference at that point — Ghidra typelock returns false in propagateTypeEdge; angr ground_truth is a fixed point) vs HINT (biases but can be overridden — type_hints, must_struct, prototype-guessed). The evidence shows type-locks are HARD but name-locks are HINT-like/cosmetic — an intentional asymmetry kuna should preserve. (3) Scope of re-run: the assertion's target artifact determines which stages re-run — the SAME edit can be narrow or full. angr makes this explicit (clears_cache flag → full S1+ re-run; reflow → narrow S5+ re-run). Ghidra's scope is always full (any edit → whole pipeline) which is correct-but-wasteful; kuna's opportunity is to inherit Ghidra's analysis but add angr-style scoped reflow by tagging each assertion with the earliest invalidated artifact. (4) Admission policy (S0 sub-stage): whether an LLM-proposed assertion is admitted as HARD ground truth or HINT — none of the tools expose a confidence-graded admission policy today, which is the key surface for LLM-agent integration (an LLM should be able to say 'I am 0.6 confident this is a char*' and have it enter as a HINT, not a lock).
hypothesis_critiques: H1 (five mechanism types) is too coarse — the evidence supports SEVEN. Beyond H1's (a) local fixed-point, (b) staged re-entry, (c) global-restart-with-hint, (d) KB reflow, (e) speculate-rollback, the corpus shows two more that don't fit any of those: (f) WORKLIST RE-ENQUEUE (Ghidra tablelist/addrlist, Reko procQueue, angr added blocks) where the re-processed unit is a data item (an address) not a stage, and (g) LAZY-DIRTY RECOMPUTE (Ghidra HighVariable coverdirty/typedirty, variable.hh:120-152) where invalidation is demand-driven and object-scoped, not a pass re-run. Folding (f)/(g) into (a)/(b) loses the scheduling distinction that matters for kuna's engine.

H1's (d) is under-specified: it treats 'outer re-decompilation against a KB' as ONE edge, but the evidence shows the SAME KB edit produces DIFFERENT scopes (angr reflow re-runs only S5-S8 via cached clinic, vs clears_cache options re-running S1+). Scope-of-re-run must be a first-class attribute of the edge, not implied. This is the single most important refinement for kuna.

H1(c) restart count is presented as a uniform mechanism, but Ghidra caps maxrestarts=1 AND gates it off during jumptable recovery (isJumptableRecoveryOn). So 'global restart' is actually a guarded, budgeted mechanism with mutual-exclusion against the worklist mechanism (f) — the model must capture that two feedback mechanisms can be mutually disabling, not freely composable.

H2 (hook points align across all three) is directionally correct and was the load-bearing premise of stage boundaries, BUT the grains differ and the taxonomy must take the FINER grain: angr's ClinicStage (0-15) + OptimizationPassStage (0-11) is far finer than Ghidra's groups, which is finer than Reko's AnalysisStage (only 4 members: PreSsa/AfterRegisterSsa/AfterStackSsa/AfterExpressionCoalescing, AnalysisContext.cs:121-142). One Ghidra group ('typerecovery') ≈ one angr stage, but Ghidra 'base'+'protorecovery' spans angr ClinicStages 0-7. Where Reko is coarse (its whole SSA+expression-building is one DataFlowAnalysis stage with ~15 internal transforms), the named-hook-boundary rule would under-segment; I deliberately used angr's finer grain to place the S2/S3/S4 boundaries, which is why S2-S4 are three stages even though Reko fuses them.

H3 (assertions never imperative) holds, but the evidence reveals it is achieved DIFFERENTLY: Ghidra/Reko persist assertions and re-run from scratch (truly declarative), while angr ALSO supports clinic_start_stage/end_stage/skip_stages — a quasi-imperative 'run only these stages' control. That is not an assertion about the artifact; it is direct pipeline control. So H3 is mostly right but the taxonomy should note a second, dev-facing control axis (stage gating) distinct from the user-facing assertion axis.

H4 (artifact-keyed stages) is strongly confirmed and is the backbone of this proposal — every feedback edge is cleanly expressible as 'stage X invalidates artifact of stage Y'. The one place it strains is angr's two-level SSA: the register-SSA artifact (S2 L0) and stack-SSA artifact (S2 L1) are arguably two artifacts, with S3/S4 partially interleaved between them (stack-pointer tracking and first callsite construction happen BETWEEN L0 and L1). I kept them inside S2 with substages, but a defensible alternative splits S2 into S2a (register definition web) and S2b (stack definition web) with S3-pre wedged between — a kuna implementation detail rather than a taxonomy flaw.
kuna_implications: ["Expose the S0 assertion store FIRST. Kuna is a Ghidra extraction, so it already HAS the richest hard-assertion surface (Symbol DB + Override: deadcodedelay, force-goto, multistage-jump, proto-override, type/name locks, union facets, isolate). The single highest-value first move is to surface these as a typed, programmatic assertion API mapped to the sub-stages above, because they already work — they are battle-tested override paths, not new code.","Add SCOPED RE-RUN, kuna's biggest differentiator. Ghidra's fatal inefficiency for an LLM-agent loop is that EVERY assertion forces a full restart (clearAnalysis + whole pipeline). Tag each assertion with the earliest artifact it invalidates (per the feedback-edge table) and implement angr-style narrow reflow: a type-lock edit should re-run S5→S8 only (like reflow_variable_types), a name edit should re-run S8 only, a force-goto should re-run S6→S8. This makes the human/LLM edit-loop interactive instead of seconds-per-edit.","Prioritize the LATENT sub-stages as the product roadmap — these are decisions Ghidra makes but does not let you override: S1.switch (angr/Reko expose explicit tables; Ghidra has JumpBasicOverride but it is awkward), S2.range-granularity (hardcoded threshold 4), S3.maxpass budget (model-internal), S4.explicit-vs-implied per-variable (heuristic-only — exposing this would massively improve readability control), S5.solver-pass-cap (compile-time 7), S6.edge-virtualization/quality (Ghidra greedily emits gotos with no rollback), S7.schema-precedence and the S7→S6 speculate-rollback (Ghidra has no SAILR-style quality gate). The S6/S7 quality-rollback is the most valuable single feature to port from angr into kuna, because it is the difference between Ghidra-grade and SAILR-grade structuring.","Map the model onto kuna's Action/Rule/group system cleanly: STAGES ≈ ActionGroups/root-action variants (the 'decompile'/'jumptable'/'paramid' root actions ARE scoped re-runs of S-subsets already — jumptable = S1-only-ish, paramid = S3-focused). SUB-STAGES ≈ individual Actions/Rules whose decision is parameterized. FEEDBACK EDGES ≈ setRestartPending + Override writes (H1c/d) and the mainloop/oppool repeat flags (H1a). Kuna should formalize the (Action, status, count) scheduling triple the report flagged and add an explicit edge-registry so each Action declares which artifact it invalidates — turning Ghidra's implicit restart_pending bit into the typed, scoped edge model above.","For LLM-agent use specifically: every sub-stage's 'intervention' field is a tool the agent can call. Build the agent surface as one function per sub-stage assertion type (assert_jump_table, assert_dead_code_delay, lock_prototype, lock_type(strength), force_goto(edge), set_name, set_explicit) with a confidence-graded admission policy (HARD vs HINT) at S0. The agent then operates the feedback edges deliberately: propose assertion → scoped re-run → read changed artifact → refine. This is exactly the loop the evidence shows humans driving today, just made first-class and cheap."]
